idiom_name: opaque struct + function-pointer dispatch table (stdio fopencookie hook style)
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the pattern is written out: a struct holds the real object (as void * or a concrete pointer), the proxy's own state (cache, counter, mutex) and a table of function pointers implementing the Subject operations; each wrapper function applies the policy and calls through the table to the real implementation. glibc's fopencookie(3) is the standard-library precedent - stdio stores a cookie_io_functions_t table and calls the caller's hooks, so a custom stream is a proxy for a FILE. Choose the hand-written table when interposing on an existing C API; when the API is already callback-based (libcurl, libuv, SQLite VFS) you normally pass wrapped callbacks instead of wrapping a struct.
pitfalls: The dispatch table must outlive the object and match the real implementation's signatures exactly; a wrong slot or a cast through void * is undefined behaviour the compiler cannot catch.
Ownership is manual and explicit: decide whether the proxy frees the real object, and make the release hook idempotent.
Lazy creation must be thread-safe (pthread_once or a mutex around the check), and the proxy state must not be copied by value.
Nothing enforces the Subject contract: proxy and real object are interchangeable only by convention, and callers can still hold the real pointer directly.
